topic.name: The Domain of a Vector-Valued Function

question.text: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf f (t) = \sqrt{4-t^2}\, \mathbf i + \ln{(t-1)}\,\mathbf j + e^t\,\mathbf k.$
question.explanation:
To find the domain of $\mathbf{f}$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

  • The domain of the 1st component $\sqrt{4-t^2}$ is $t \in [-2,2].$

  • The domain of the 2nd component $\ln{(t-1)}$ is $t \in (1,\infty).$

  • The domain of the 3rd component $e^t$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(t)$ is $t \in (1,2].$

example.title: Domains of Functions With Exponential and Logarithmic Components

question.text: The domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf f (t) = \cos t\, \mathbf i + \sqrt{2+t^2} \,\mathbf j + \cot t\,\mathbf k$ is \[ t\in (-\infty,\infty), \quad t \neq \bbox[5pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}. \] What is the missing expression? You may assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
To find the domain of $\mathbf{f}$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

  • The domain of the 1st component $\cos t$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

  • The domain of the 2nd component $\sqrt{2+t^2}$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

  • The domain of the 3rd component $\cot t$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty)$, $t \neq n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(t)$ is \[ t\in (-\infty,\infty), \quad t \neq \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}n\pi}, \] where $n$ is an integer.

example.title: Domains of Functions With Trigonometric Components

question.text: The domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf f (t) = 2t^3\, \mathbf i +(1+\cos{t})\,\mathbf j + \sec{t}\,\mathbf k$ is \[ t\in (-\infty,\infty), \quad t \neq \bbox[5pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}. \] What is the missing expression? You may assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
To find the domain of $\mathbf{f}$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

  • The domain of the 1st component $2t^3$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

  • The domain of the 2nd component $1 + \cos t$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

  • The domain of the 3rd component $\sec t$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty)$, $t \neq \dfrac{\pi}{2}+n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(t)$ is \[ t\in (-\infty,\infty), \quad t \neq \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}\dfrac{\pi}{2}+n\pi}, \] where $n$ is an integer.

example.title: Domains of Functions With Trigonometric Components

question.text: The domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf f (t) = (1-\cot{t})\, \mathbf i + \sin{2t} \,\mathbf j + t^2\,\mathbf k$ is \[ t\in (-\infty,\infty), \quad t \neq \bbox[5pt, border:1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAA}}. \] What is the missing expression? You may assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.explanation:
To find the domain of $\mathbf{f}$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

  • The domain of the 1st component $1-\cot{t}$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty),$ , $t \neq n\pi,$ where $n$ is an integer.

  • The domain of the 2nd component $\sin{2t}$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

  • The domain of the 3rd component $t^2$ is $t \in (-\infty,\infty).$

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(t)$ is \[ t\in (-\infty,\infty), \quad t \neq \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\color{blue}n\pi}, \] where $n$ is an integer.

example.title: Domains of Functions With Trigonometric Components

question.text: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf f(s) = \ln(s-2) \, \mathbf i + (1-s) \, \mathbf j + s^2 \,\mathbf k.$
question.explanation:
To find the domain of $\mathbf{f}$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

  • The domain of the 1st component $\ln(s-2)$ is $s \in (2,\infty).$

  • The domain of the 2nd component $1-s$ is $s \in (-\infty, \infty).$

  • The domain of the 3rd component $s^2$ is $s \in (-\infty,\infty).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}(s)$ is $s \in (2,\infty).$
